skill_traces.query:
Evan: Hey Sam, how's it going? Been a while since we talked. Hope all is good.
Sam: Hey Evan! It's been a rough week - I gave in and bought some unhealthy snacks. I feel kinda guilty. How's it going for you? That painting is awesome! Did you paint it?
Evan: Hey Sam, sorry to hear about the rough week. Don't worry about the snacks. I'm doing okay, just finished this painting of a sunset. It really helps me relax. So, how's everything going with you? Anything new and exciting?
Sam: Thanks, Evan! Yeah, I just couldn't resist them. Gotta do better. As for me, just dealing with work stress and trying to stay motivated.
Evan: Hey Sam, work stress can really get to you. Have you tried anything new to de-stress? Maybe picking up a hobby or something could help.
Sam: Thinking about trying something different outdoors. Any suggestions?
Evan: Sounds good! Have you ever tried kayaking? It's a fun and active way to paddle on a river or lake. What are your thoughts on that?
Sam: Kayaking sounds awesome! Haven't tried it yet, but it looks like a fun way to get in some exercise and enjoy nature. I'm definitely considering giving it a try. Thanks!
Evan: No worries, Sam! It's a fun way to get in some exercise and enjoy nature. Let me know when you're ready to give it a try and I can hook you up with a good spot.
Sam: Thanks for the idea, my mate and I are just around the corner from kayaking on the lake, we're going to try that now!
Evan: Of course, let me know if you like it, we can plan a kayaking trip together, I'll pick a cool spot!
Sam: Yep, Evan! Can't wait. Thanks for the help!
Evan: Ready for an adventure? Where will you go?
Sam: We're traveling through Lake Tahoe! I heard it's great for kayaking.
Evan: Hey Sam, it's an awesome pick! You'll love it there - clear water and gorgeous views. Have a blast and take lots of pics!
Sam: Thanks, Evan! I'm looking forward to it!

selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains offers of help and encouragement, such as Evan offering to hook Sam up with a good kayaking spot and suggesting a kayaking trip together.

selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.
selected.rerank_reason: The session includes specific details about the planned activity (kayaking on Lake Tahoe) and the participants' intentions, which should be captured in the event memory content.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture Brief Project Mentions with Full Attributes
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a speaker mentions a project they completed, are working on, or plan to build, even briefly.
content: Create an event candidate for any explicit statement of a completed, ongoing, or planned project, even in small talk.
When several messages describe the same project, consolidate them into one candidate and include every explicit attribute stated.
Stop once the speaker has finished describing the project in that session.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.
